title: Fix fine-tuning on supported PyTorch 2.2 versions
body:
## Problem

Fine-tuning raises `AttributeError: module 'torch' has no attribute 'GradScaler'` on PyTorch 2.2, although `pyproject.toml` supports `torch>=2.2`. This happens even on CPU or with `amp=False`, because `_make_amp` constructs a scaler unconditionally.

## Change

Prefer the existing `torch.GradScaler` API when available. On PyTorch 2.2, fall back to `torch.cuda.amp.GradScaler(enabled=use_amp)`, which provides the same scaler operations. Keep AMP enablement and autocast behavior unchanged.

The fallback uses the [PyTorch 2.2 CUDA scaler API](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/v2.2.2/torch/cuda/amp/grad_scaler.py), including its different constructor signature. No dependency minimum is raised.

## Validation

`python -m pytest tests/test_finetune_amp.py tests/test_finetune_freezing.py tests/test_finetune_early_stopping.py tests/test_finetune_string_input.py -q`: **26 passed** on Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.2.2 CPU, using the official classifier and regressor checkpoints.

- All **19 existing fine-tuning tests fail on upstream main** with the missing-GradScaler exception and pass with this change. These exercise actual model training, freezing, early stopping and categorical inputs.
- Four new tests exercise a real CPU backward/optimizer step through the legacy scaler for both estimators, with `amp=True` and `amp=False`.
- Two tests check legacy CUDA scaler enablement through lazy construction with CUDA availability mocked; actual GPU training was not run on this machine.
- One test checks that the modern API remains preferred when available (simulated on the installed PyTorch 2.2 runtime).
- The six new legacy-path tests fail before the fix. Ruff checks and `git diff --check` pass.

title: Restore PyTorch thread count when prediction fails
body:
## Problem

When `n_jobs` is set, both estimators change the process-wide PyTorch thread count during prediction. The previous value is restored only after successful inference. A feature-count validation error, preprocessing exception or model-forward failure therefore leaves subsequent PyTorch work running with the estimator's thread limit.

For example, with `torch.set_num_threads(2)` and a fitted estimator using `n_jobs=1`, calling prediction with the wrong number of columns raises `ValueError` and leaves `torch.get_num_threads() == 1`.

## Change

Move the existing thread-selection logic into a shared private decorator, restoring the caller's setting with `try/finally`. Apply it to classifier `predict_proba` and regressor `predict`; classifier `predict` delegates to `predict_proba`.

The `n_jobs=None` path does not modify thread settings. Positive/negative limits and the warning when exceeding the logical CPU count are preserved. This fixes cleanup after failed calls; it does not introduce synchronization for concurrent calls sharing PyTorch's global setting.

## Validation

`python -m pytest tests/test_prediction_threads.py tests/test_sklearn.py tests/test_numpy_inputs.py tests/test_predict_allnan_categorical.py -q`: **209 passed, 364 skipped** on CPU, Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.2.2. Skips include unavailable accelerator backends.

- All **12 exception-restoration cases fail on upstream main**, covering validation, encoding and inference, with and without caches, for both estimators.
- New tests cover thread selection, warnings, successful restoration, and recovery after invalid input using official checkpoints with no cache, KV cache and representation cache.
- A separate comparison against the original upstream prediction methods on **9 official-checkpoint configurations** produced bit-identical outputs, including both classifier ensemble modes and all four regressor output types.
- Ruff checks for the new tests, syntax/error checks for modified modules and `git diff --check` pass.

Related: #158 also refactors classifier inference. These PRs are independently based on main but overlap in that method. When combining them, the decorator should wrap `_predict_ensemble` so both `predict_proba` and `predict_logits` restore the thread count.

The resolution is prepared on the [combined validation branch](https://github.com/ayoubchikri/tabicl/tree/verify/contributions), together with #159 and #161. Its four focused test modules pass **92 tests**, including two additional checks for `predict_logits` thread restoration after invalid input. This branch is provided for integration reference; the PR itself contains only the thread-restoration fix and its tests.

title: Allow user-provided backgrounds for SHAP explanations
body:
## Summary

Allow users to explain predictions relative to a reference dataset by passing the keyword-only `X_background` argument to `get_shap_values` or `get_shap_explainer`. The existing single all-NaN background remains the default.

Closes #117.

Backgrounds accept numeric arrays, lists and DataFrames, with validation for dimensionality, nonempty samples and matching feature counts. The API documentation explains consistent encoding/column order and background selection.

## Validation

`python -m pytest tests/test_shap_background.py tests/test_shap_categorical.py -q`: **20 passed** on CPU (Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.2.2, SHAP 0.49.1).

- Exact SHAP values and expected reference predictions checked analytically for a linear model, including default-background compatibility and DataFrame feature names.
- Additivity and reference predictions checked with the official TabICL v2 classifier and regressor checkpoints.
- Invalid backgrounds produce actionable errors; input backgrounds are not mutated.
- The three array/list/DataFrame reference tests fail on upstream main because `X_background` is forwarded as an unsupported SHAP constructor argument.
- Ruff checks for the new tests and syntax/error checks for the modified module pass; `git diff --check` passes.

title: Add predict_logits to TabICLClassifier
body:
## Summary

Expose classifier logits for interpretation with SHAP/ShapIQ, implementing the approach discussed in #126 with the original reporter and maintainer.

- Share the existing ensemble inference path between `predict_proba` and `predict_logits`.
- Preserve averaged model logits when `average_logits=True`; otherwise return `softmax_temperature * log(averaged probabilities)`, clipping zero probabilities to keep scores finite.
- Document temperature scaling, class ordering, hierarchical classification, and ShapIQ's automatic preference for logits. Existing `predict_proba` results are preserved.

Fixes #126.

## Validation

- **22 new tests pass**, including actual small-model inference with both ensemble modes, two temperatures, both cache types, class shuffling, missing values, hierarchical classification, and SHAP/ShapIQ integration.
- **28 configurations with the official v2 classifier checkpoint**: probabilities are bit-identical to upstream `0dbff3e`. Applying softmax to the returned logits divided by temperature recovers probabilities with maximum absolute error `1.2e-7`.
- Three API tests fail against upstream because `predict_logits` is absent, and pass with this change.
- Ruff on the new tests and `git diff --check` pass.

Local environment: macOS Intel, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.2.2. The full suite reports **236 passed, 379 skipped, 19 failed**. All 19 failures are the same pre-existing fine-tuning failures reproduced on upstream: this PyTorch version lacks `torch.GradScaler`. CUDA/XPU/MPS validation is left to the project CI.

The pre-existing PyTorch 2.2 fine-tuning failures are addressed separately in #161: all 19 existing fine-tuning tests pass with that compatibility fix.

Implementation and tests were developed with AI assistance; the validation above was executed.

title: Enhance docstring with notes on group generation
body:
This PR documents the connection between TabICL’s repeated feature-grouping scheme and Golomb rulers.

In "same" mode, feature groups are generated using circular shifts whose offsets have distinct pairwise differences. Up to translation, this corresponds to a Golomb-ruler construction such as (0, 1, 3, 7, ...), which explains why a given pair of features is not repeated across groups.

The change only updates the docstring/documentation and adds the relevant reference; there is no change to the implementation or model behavior.

title: Keep reserved column slots at skip_value when target_aware=True
body:
Fixes Issue #155.

The y embeddings are only added to columns that are not indicated as skippable with skip_value.

---

## Verifications by Claude

- **Logits are bit-identical.** Released `tabicl-classifier-v2-20260212.ckpt`, `n_estimators=1`, `T=1000` tables at 5 to 50 features: `max |Δlogit| = 0.0`. Expected, since `RowInteraction` overwrites `embeddings[:, :, :num_cls]` unconditionally in both forward paths (`_model/interaction.py:201`, `:248`), so the reserved slots were being discarded anyway.
- **The fast path now fires.** Counting the ISAB calls in which `(src == skip_value).all(dim=(-2, -1))` is true: 0 of 12 as shipped, 12 of 12 with the fix, on the same runs. As shipped, the reserved slots leave the column stage as noise in the range `-100.59` to `-99.38`, not `-100.0`.
- **The invariant holds in every branch.** Reserved slots leave `ColEmbedding` as exactly `skip_value`, and feature slots never do, for all six paths through `_compute_embeddings`: not target-aware, target-aware, mixed-radix, regression, without feature grouping, and without feature grouping with `d` given. Five of those six fail without this patch.

`ColEmbedding` at the released v2 config, `T=1000`, `train_size=800`, CPU:

```
features  fired (shipped)  fired (fixed)   shipped    fixed  speedup  feature slots identical
       5              0/3            3/3    0.027s   0.018s    1.53x                     True
      10              0/3            3/3    0.041s   0.031s    1.30x                     True
      25              0/3            3/3    0.083s   0.074s    1.13x                     True
      50              0/3            3/3    0.155s   0.149s    1.04x                     True
     100              0/3            3/3    0.296s   0.293s    1.01x                     True
```

The saving is `reserve_cls_tokens / (reserve_cls_tokens + G)` of stage-one compute, since the group axis is folded into the batch: roughly 44% of the column stage on a 5-feature table and 4% on a 100-feature one. End to end that is about 1.05x to 1.1x up to 25 features and within noise beyond.

The cache path is left alone. `_compute_embeddings_with_cache` destroys the sentinel the same way, but `forward_with_cache` (`_model/layers.py:787`) keeps the batch dimensions for the cache and cannot skip, so there are no FLOPs to save there.

title: Column-stage fast path is never taken when `target_aware=True'
body:
While reimplementing the TabICL v2 column stage I noticed that the `skip_value` fast path for the CLS columns is never taken when `target_aware=True`.

CLS columns are initialized with a skip value (`-100`), signalling that for this column the attention computation can be skipped. When `target_aware=True`, this skip value is overwritten, and the fast path is never taken. This does not affect the output of the model, only its computational efficiency.

A Claude-generated, more detailed description of the issue can be found below. I will open a PR with a fix.

## Summary by Claude

`ColEmbedding._compute_embeddings` (`_model/embedding.py:372-390`) does:

```python
src = self.in_linear(features)                                 # SkippableLinear -> reserved slots are exactly -100
...
src[..., :train_size, :] = src[..., :train_size, :] + y_emb    # embedding.py:389
src = self.tf_col(src, train_size=...)
```

and the guard it feeds is (`_model/layers.py:673`):

```python
skip_mask = (src == self.skip_value).all(dim=(-2, -1))
```

The guard requires *every* row and channel of a slice to equal `-100.0`. Adding `y_emb` to the first `train_size` rows breaks that for every reserved slot, so `skip_mask.any()` is `False` from line 389 onward and the fast path is dead.

The `not self.target_aware` branch three lines earlier calls `tf_col` directly after `in_linear`, where the guard works as intended — so this looks like the target-aware path having invalidated an optimisation written for the other one, rather than dead code.

### Evidence

Measured by wrapping `InducedSelfAttentionBlock.forward` to count how often its skip guard is true, with `ColEmbedding` built at the released v2 config and random weights (the branch taken does not depend on trained weights), `T=1000`, `train_size=800`, tabicl 2.2.0 on CPU:

```
features  fired (shipped)  fired (fixed)   shipped    fixed  speedup  feature slots identical
       5              0/3            3/3    0.027s   0.018s    1.53x                     True
      10              0/3            3/3    0.041s   0.031s    1.30x                     True
      25              0/3            3/3    0.083s   0.074s    1.13x                     True
      50              0/3            3/3    0.155s   0.149s    1.04x                     True
     100              0/3            3/3    0.296s   0.293s    1.01x                     True
```

`fired` counts ISAB calls in which `skip_mask.any()` was true: 0 of 3 as shipped, 3 of 3 with the fix. What the reserved slots actually contain on the way out of the shipped column stage is noise near the sentinel (range `-100.59 .. -99.38`), not `-100.0`.

Wasted work is `reserve_cls_tokens / (reserve_cls_tokens + G)` of stage-one compute, since the group axis is folded into the batch — ~44% on a 5-feature table, ~4% on a 100-feature one. End-to-end with the real `tabicl-classifier-v2-20260212.ckpt` checkpoint (`n_estimators=1`, same `T=1000` tables, 5–50 features) the fast path fires 0/12 times as shipped and 12/12 with the fix, the whole-model speedup on CPU is ~1.05x–1.1x up to 25 features and within timing noise at 50, and the logits are **bit-identical** (`max |Δlogit| = 0.0`), because `RowInteraction` overwrites `embeddings[:, :, :num_cls]` unconditionally in both forward paths (`_model/interaction.py:201`, `:248`).

### Scope

Paths I checked in 2.2.0 (line numbers identical in 2.1.1):

| path | status |
|---|---|
| `_compute_embeddings`, `target_aware=True`, standard branch (`embedding.py:389`) | fast path dead — this is the released config |
| `_compute_embeddings`, mixed-radix branch (`embedding.py:409`) | same pattern, same effect |
| `_train_forward_without_feature_group` with `d` given | routes through `_compute_embeddings`, same |
| `_compute_embeddings_with_cache`, `store_cache=True` (`embedding.py:789`) | sentinel also destroyed, but `forward_with_cache` (`layers.py:787`) deliberately keeps batch dims for the cache and only restores the value, so no FLOPs are lost there |
| `_compute_embeddings_with_cache`, `use_cache=True` | no `y_emb` addition, sentinel survives |
| `target_aware=False` | fires as intended |

So the fix belongs in `_compute_embeddings` (both branches); the cache path would only gain consistency, not speed, and the PR leaves it alone.

### Environment

tabicl 2.2.0 (first seen on 2.1.1) · torch 2.13.0 · Python 3.12.13 · macOS 26.6.2 (arm64), CPU

title: Use grad scaler for float32 + FlashAttention-3
body: Fixes https://github.com/soda-inria/tabicl/issues/153

title: GradScaler is disabled for float32 pre-training although FlashAttention-3 internally uses float16
body:
```markdown
## Description

PR #151 changed the pre-training `GradScaler` configuration from:
self.scaler = torch.GradScaler("cuda", enabled=self.amp)
```

to:

```python
self.scaler = torch.GradScaler(
    "cuda",
    enabled=self.amp and amp_dtype == torch.float16,
)
```

This is correct for a model whose numerical precision is determined entirely by the global autocast dtype. However, this is not the case for the current FlashAttention-3 implementation.

The official TabICLv2 Stage 2 and Stage 3 scripts use:

```bash
--dtype float32
--use_flash_attn3 True
```

Therefore, after PR #151, `GradScaler` is disabled in these stages.

However, `sdpa_with_flattened_batch()` explicitly converts float32 Q/K/V tensors to float16 before calling FlashAttention-3:

```python
orig_dtype = q.dtype

if orig_dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
    fa_dtype = torch.float16
else:
    fa_dtype = orig_dtype

q_fa = q.transpose(...).contiguous().to(fa_dtype)
k_fa = k.transpose(...).contiguous().to(fa_dtype)
v_fa = v.transpose(...).contiguous().to(fa_dtype)

out = flash_attn3(q_fa, k_fa, v_fa, ...)
out = out.to(orig_dtype)
```

Consequently, the effective Stage 2/3 computation is not pure float32:

```text
float32 model
        ↓
Q/K/V explicitly cast to float16
        ↓
FlashAttention-3 forward and backward in float16
        ↓
output / gradients converted back to float32
```

The conversion back to float32 cannot recover gradient values that have already underflowed during the float16 FlashAttention-3 backward pass.

## Observed behavior

I tested the official Stage 2/3-style configuration with:

```bash
--dtype float32
--use_flash_attn3 True
```

The results are:

- With the previous behavior, where `GradScaler` remained enabled, pre-training works normally.
- With the new PR #151 behavior, where `GradScaler` is disabled because `--dtype` is `float32`, pre-training quality deteriorates substantially.
- Restoring the previous `GradScaler` behavior resolves the degradation.

Stage 1 is not affected in the same way because the official Stage 1 recipe uses:

```bash
--use_flash_attn3 False
```

## Why the current condition is insufficient

The current condition assumes that only global float16 autocast requires loss scaling:

```python
enabled=self.amp and amp_dtype == torch.float16
```

However, `config.dtype` only describes the autocast dtype. It does not describe all low-precision operations in the computation graph.

Even with `--dtype float32`, FlashAttention-3 introduces differentiable float16 operations through its explicit Q/K/V casts. Loss scaling is therefore still needed to protect the backward pass from float16 gradient underflow.

This also explains why the previous apparently redundant behavior:

```python
enabled=self.amp
```

was beneficial for the official Stage 2/3 float32 recipe.

## Expected behavior

`GradScaler` should be enabled whenever the actual computation graph contains a float16 training path, including when:

```text
--dtype float32
--use_flash_attn3 True
```

It should remain disabled for a genuine bfloat16-only path.

## Minimal workaround

Restoring the previous behavior fixes the issue for the current TabICLv2 recipes:

```diff
- self.scaler = torch.GradScaler(
-     "cuda",
-     enabled=self.amp and amp_dtype == torch.float16,
- )
+ self.scaler = torch.GradScaler(
+     "cuda",
+     enabled=self.amp,
+ )
```

This is the smallest and safest change for the existing Stage 2/3 recipes.

## Possible precise fix

A more precise implementation could distinguish global float16 autocast from the internal float32-to-float16 conversion performed by FlashAttention-3:

```python
self.amp = self.config.amp and "cuda" in self.config.device

model_compute_dtype = amp_dtype if self.amp else torch.float32

uses_fp16_autocast = self.amp and amp_dtype == torch.float16

uses_fp16_fa3 = (
    HAS_FLASH_ATTN3
    and self.config.use_flash_attn3
    and "cuda" in self.config.device
    and model_compute_dtype == torch.float32
)

enable_grad_scaler = uses_fp16_autocast or uses_fp16_fa3

self.scaler = torch.GradScaler(
    "cuda",
    enabled=enable_grad_scaler,
)
```

The intended behavior would then be:

| Effective computation path | GradScaler |
|---|---:|
| Float32 without FA3 | Disabled |
| Float32 model + float16 FA3 | Enabled |
| Float16 autocast | Enabled |
| BFloat16 model + bfloat16 FA3 | Disabled |

title: Keep one constant feature so all-constant X fits instead of raising
body:
## Problem

When every feature in `X` is constant, `fit` fails with an opaque error from an internal recursion helper:

```
IndexError: Cannot choose from an empty sequence
```

Constant columns are dropped by `UniqueFeatureFilter`, so when *all* of them are constant the matrix reaches `Shuffler` with `n_features_in_ = 0`. `_latin_squares` → `_rls` handles `n == 1` but not `n == 0`, and bottoms out in `random.choice` on an empty list.

Repro:

```python
import numpy as np
from tabicl import TabICLRegressor

X = np.array([[0.4, 1.0, 0.5, 118.2],
              [0.4, 1.0, 0.5, 118.2]])   # every column constant
y = np.array([-3.2, -1.0])

TabICLRegressor(n_estimators=4, random_state=0).fit(X, y)
```

## Behaviour

`UniqueFeatureFilter` keeps the first feature when every one of them would be removed, so `n_features_in_` is never 0. Constant features are still dropped whenever at least one informative feature remains; only the all-constant case is affected.

The model then sees a single uninformative column and falls back to the marginal distribution of the target, as sklearn estimators do in this situation:

```python
X = np.tile(np.array([0.4, 1.0, 0.5, 118.2]), (6, 1))
y = np.array([-3.2, -1.0, 0.5, 2.0, -0.7, 1.1])

TabICLRegressor(n_estimators=4, random_state=0).fit(X, y).predict(X)
# array([-0.1974, -0.1974, ...])   y.mean() = -0.2167

TabICLClassifier(n_estimators=4, random_state=0).fit(X, [0,1,0,1,1,0]).predict_proba(X)
# array([[0.5, 0.5], ...])         the base rate
```

Every stage downstream tolerates zero variance already: `CustomStandardScaler` adds `epsilon` to the standard deviation and `OutlierRemover` floors it at `1e-6`, so the kept column reaches the model as a constant token — exactly `0.0` for both `norm_method='none'` and `'power'`, with no warnings.

## Tests

One test: all-constant `X` fits and returns the marginal, and constant features are still dropped when an informative one remains.

`tests/test_numpy_inputs.py tests/test_sklearn.py` → 280 passed, 244 skipped (skips are cuda/xpu/mps).

## Note

With a constant training column, a *test* row carrying a different constant maps to a large z-score before clipping (the scaler divides by `1e-6`), so predictions sit near the training marginal rather than pinned to it — `-0.197` at the training value, `-1.012` at `-500`, against `y.mean() = -0.217` and `y.std() = 1.70`. Pinning it exactly would mean zeroing the kept column outright, which seemed like extra machinery for a case where the answer carries no information — happy to add it if preferred.

title: predict_proba crashes with IndexError when a column is all-NaN
body:
Hi! Ran into a crash using `TabICLClassifier` on a real dataset where one of the feature columns happened to be entirely NaN (an all-NULL column that came straight out of a SQL sample).

`fit()` accepts the data without complaints, but `predict_proba()` then fails with:

```
File .../tabicl/_sklearn/preprocessing.py, line 1143, in transform
    filtered_mask = feature_mask[self.unique_filter_.features_to_keep_]
IndexError: boolean index did not match indexed array along axis 0; size of axis is 9 but size of corresponding boolean axis is 8
```

Minimal repro (tabicl 2.1.1):

```python
import numpy as np
from tabicl import TabICLClassifier

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
X = rng.normal(size=(200, 9))
X[:, 8] = np.nan                      # one all-NaN column
y = (X[:, 0] > 0).astype(int)

clf = TabICLClassifier(random_state=0)
clf.fit(X[:150], y[:150])             # works (just a sklearn warning)
clf.predict_proba(X[150:])            # IndexError
```

What seems to happen: the default `SimpleImputer` silently drops the all-NaN column during fit, so the internal feature filter is fitted on 8 columns — but at predict time the NaN feature mask is built from the original 9-column input, and the two no longer line up.

The fix looks like a one-liner: passing `keep_empty_features=True` to the `SimpleImputer` in `src/tabicl/_sklearn/preprocessing.py` keeps the column count stable end to end (the constant-feature filter then drops the column through its normal path). I've tested this locally — with the change, all-NaN columns work in both fit and predict, numpy and DataFrame inputs alike.

Possibly related to #143, which also involves all-NaN columns at predict time (categorical there, numeric here).

Happy to open a PR with the fix + a small regression test if useful.

title: Respect cgroup memory limits when detecting available CPU memory
body:
## The problem

`InferenceManager.get_available_cpu_memory()` returns `psutil.virtual_memory().available`, which reports the **host's** free memory and is blind to cgroup limits. Inside a memory-limited container — Docker, Kubernetes, most GPU clouds — it can substantially overstate what the process may actually allocate.

Measured on the container where I hit this:

| | |
|---|---:|
| `psutil.virtual_memory().available` | **450.8 GB** |
| cgroup limit | 116.4 GB |
| cgroup already used | 14.0 GB |
| **real headroom** | **102.4 GB** |

A 4.4× overestimate. `free` reports the same host figure, which is why this is easy to misdiagnose from inside the container.

## Why it matters

That value feeds `_resolve_offload_mode(output_mb, gpu_mem, cpu_free, disk_free)`, which decides whether `offload="auto"` keeps outputs in CPU memory or escalates to disk. Believing it has 450 GB, it never escalates.

The resulting failure is unusually hard to diagnose: the cgroup OOM killer sends **SIGKILL**, so the process dies with **no Python traceback and no CUDA error**. From the outside it is indistinguishable from a clean exit — the script simply moves on to the next thing.

In my case it cost two multi-hour runs before I attributed it. Both completed an *entire* validation sweep and died at the first larger prediction, which is what finally gave it away: the same process, the same task, minutes apart, with the GPU holding 1 MiB at the moment of death. It was never VRAM.

## The fix

Intersect the cgroup headroom with psutil's figure rather than replacing it:

```python
available = psutil.virtual_memory().available
headroom = _cgroup_memory_headroom()
if headroom is not None:
    available = min(available, headroom)
```

So the estimate can **only ever become more conservative**. On a host without a cgroup limit the returned value is unchanged.

`_cgroup_memory_headroom()`:

- handles cgroup **v2** (`memory.max` / `memory.current`) and **v1** (`memory.limit_in_bytes` / `memory.usage_in_bytes`)
- returns `None` for v2's literal `"max"`, for v1's ~2**63 "unlimited" sentinel, and for any limit at or above physical memory
- **never raises** — a memory estimate is not worth failing an inference call over, so every error path falls back to the previous behaviour

## Tests

Six in `tests/test_inference_memory.py`: no cgroup present, limit-minus-usage, both unlimited sentinels, permission errors, and one pinning that the returned value can only shrink relative to psutil's.

## Scope — what this does not fix

This corrects the *detection*; it does not make every workload fit. After this change one of my tasks (≈255k inference rows × 342 features) still OOMs even with `offload="disk"`, and one that previously died now completes. I mention it so the change is not read as a general fix for large-input OOMs.

Happy to adjust naming, placement, or the cgroup-reading approach if you'd prefer it structured differently.

title: predict_proba crashes when a categorical column is all-NaN in the prediction batch
body:
When every value of a `category`-dtype column is missing in the batch passed to `predict_proba`, the masked-feature fill in `_sklearn/classifier.py` writes the float `0.0` into that column:

https://github.com/soda-inria/tabicl/blob/main/tabicl/_sklearn/classifier.py (v2.1.1, around line 740):

```python
# Fill masked columns so that transformers don't choke on NaN
if feature_mask is not None:
    if hasattr(X, "columns"):  # Proxy way to check whether X is a dataframe
        X.iloc[:, feature_mask] = 0.0
```

For a categorical column this emits a pandas FutureWarning (`Value '0.0' has dtype incompatible with category`), leaves the column in a state the fitted `X_encoder_` can't transform, and `predict_proba` then raises:

```
TypeError: ufunc 'isnan' not supported for the input types, and the inputs could not be safely coerced to any supported types according to the casting rule ''safe''
```

Under pandas 3 the incompatible-dtype assignment itself becomes an error, so the fill will fail even earlier.

## Reproducer (tabicl 2.1.1, pandas 2.2.3)

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from tabicl import TabICLClassifier

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
n = 200
X = pd.DataFrame({
    "num": rng.normal(size=n),
    "cat": pd.Categorical(rng.choice(["a", "b", "c"], size=n)),
})
y = pd.Series(rng.choice([0, 1], size=n))

clf = TabICLClassifier(n_estimators=1)
clf.fit(X, y)

X_pred = X.head(20).copy()
X_pred["cat"] = pd.Categorical([None] * 20, categories=["a", "b", "c"])  # all-NaN in the batch
clf.predict_proba(X_pred)  # TypeError: ufunc 'isnan' not supported ...
```

## Real-world impact

This is not a synthetic corner: in an AutoGluon benchmark run over 121 datasets (8-fold bagging, TabICLv2 checkpoints), the out-of-fold prediction step hit this on 5 datasets - a categorical column that happens to be entirely missing within one validation fold is enough - and the model was skipped on those datasets entirely.

## Suggested direction

The fill needs to be dtype-aware for DataFrames. One option is to replace the masked columns wholesale so the dtype changes with the assignment (the columns are all-NaN, so no information is lost):

```python
masked_cols = X.columns[feature_mask]
X[masked_cols] = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=X.index, columns=masked_cols)
```

title: Fix: isnan/isfinite
body:
I think this fixes a probable bug where invalid (`inf`) values could enter the generation procedure.
Example to generate about 1024 `inf` datasets:

```python
import torch, numpy as np
from tabicl.prior import PriorDataset
from tabicl.prior._mlp_scm import MLPSCM
from tabicl.prior._tree_scm import TreeSCM

N = 100_000  # num draws

def _f(self):  # same code as forward in the prior package
    causes = self.xsampler.sample()  # (seq_len, num_causes)
    outputs = [causes]
    for layer in self.layers:
        outputs.append(layer(outputs[-1]))
    outputs = outputs[2:]  # Start from 2 because the first layer is only linear without activation
    X, y = self.handle_outputs(causes, outputs)

    # HERE we introduced the change
    if torch.any(torch.isnan(X)) or torch.any(torch.isnan(y)):
        X[:] = 0.0
        y[:] = -100.0

    if self.num_outputs == 1:
        y = y.squeeze(-1)
    return X, y


# monkeypatched for easy check
MLPSCM.forward = _f
TreeSCM.forward = _f

np.random.seed(0); torch.manual_seed(0)
prior = PriorDataset(
    regression=True, batch_size=8, batch_size_per_gp=8,
    batch_size_per_subgp=8, min_features=2, max_features=64,
    max_seq_len=1024, min_train_size=0.25, max_train_size=0.9,
    prior_type="mlp_scm", device="cpu", n_jobs=1)

for i, batch in enumerate(prior):
    print(f"\r{i}", end="", flush=True)
    if i >= N: break
    X, y, d, _, _ = batch
    if not torch.isfinite(y).all():
        n_inf = (~torch.isfinite(y)).sum().item()
        bad_tables = (~torch.isfinite(y)).any(1)
        print(f"{i=}: {n_inf=}")
        for t in range(len(y)):
            if not torch.isfinite(y[t]).all():
                n_nan = torch.isnan(y[t]).sum().item()
                n_inf = torch.isinf(y[t]).sum().item()
                print(f"{t=}: {n_nan=}, {n_inf=}, {y.shape[1]=}")
        break
```

title: Fix UnicodeEncodeError in fine-tuning tutorials on Windows
body:
## Problem

Both fine-tuning tutorials crash on Windows. Training completes fine, then the script dies while printing the results table:

```
File "tutorials/finetune_regressor.py", line 135, in <module>
    print(header)
UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character '\u0394' in position 51: character maps to <undefined>
```

On Windows `sys.stdout` defaults to the legacy code page (cp1252), which cannot encode `U+0394` (Δ), `U+2191` (↑) or `U+2193` (↓).

The crash lands *after* `fit()` but *before* the figures are drawn, so all fine-tuning work is lost and neither figure is produced — the tutorial appears to fail entirely despite the model having trained successfully.

Affects `tutorials/finetune_classifier.py` and `tutorials/finetune_regressor.py`. The other six tutorials are unaffected: they print pure ASCII, except `getting_started.py`, whose `R²` happens to be encodable in cp1252.

## Fix

Restrict the printed table to ASCII: `Δ` → `delta`, and the per-metric `↑`/`↓` arrows are replaced by a single legend line stating the direction of improvement.

Non-ASCII elsewhere in these files is deliberately left alone — axis labels, titles and `metric_names` only ever reach Matplotlib, which renders text itself and is unaffected by the console code page.

## Verification

Run on Windows 11, `sys.stdout.encoding == 'cp1252'`, no `PYTHONIOENCODING` override. Before this change both tutorials raised `UnicodeEncodeError`; after it, both run to completion and emit both figures:

```
======================================================
Test-set metrics  (n_train=80, n_test=1220)
======================================================
metric          pretrained    fine-tuned         delta
------------------------------------------------------
ROC-AUC             0.9790        0.9906       +0.0116
log-loss            0.1880        0.1238       -0.0642
accuracy            0.9057        0.9410       +0.0352
======================================================
higher is better: ROC-AUC, accuracy;  lower is better: log-loss
```

CI does not catch this because the runners use UTF-8 stdout, and the tutorials are not executed as tests.

title: DatetimeEncoder sin/cos encoding is off by one, causing angle collisions
body:
`tabicl.forecast.transforms.DatetimeEncoder.generate()` encodes seasonal features as sin/cos pairs. By dividing by (p-1) instead of p, where p is the period length, the first and last elements of the period are mapped to the same angle.

Problematic line is: https://github.com/soda-inria/tabicl/blob/46b91961db4f8873dd049ec09990698a435e1e29/src/tabicl/forecast/transforms/_calendar.py#L93

## Steps to reproduce

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import gluonts.time_feature as tf

ts = pd.date_range("2011-01-01", periods=24 * 3, freq="h")  # Sat, Sun, Mon
dow = tf.day_of_week_index(ts).astype(int)

p = 7
adjusted = p - 1  # this causes the issue
sin = np.sin(2 * np.pi * dow / adjusted)
cos = np.cos(2 * np.pi * dow / adjusted)

for h in [0, 23, 24, 47, 48]:
    print(ts[h], "dow=", dow[h], "sin=", round(sin[h], 3), "cos=", round(cos[h], 3))
```

Output:

```
2011-01-01 00:00:00 dow= 5 sin= -0.866 cos= 0.5
2011-01-01 23:00:00 dow= 5 sin= -0.866 cos= 0.5
2011-01-02 00:00:00 dow= 6 sin= -0.0 cos= 1.0
2011-01-02 23:00:00 dow= 6 sin= -0.0 cos= 1.0
2011-01-03 00:00:00 dow= 0 sin= 0.0 cos= 1.0 <- This is identical to Sunday (dow=6)
```

The same collision happens with other seasonal sin/cos features like day_of_the_year.

## Expected behavior


```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import gluonts.time_feature as tf

ts = pd.date_range("2011-01-01", periods=24 * 3, freq="h")  # Sat, Sun, Mon
dow = tf.day_of_week_index(ts).astype(int)

p = 7
sin = np.sin(2 * np.pi * dow / p)
cos = np.cos(2 * np.pi * dow / p)

for h in [0, 23, 24, 47, 48]:
    print(ts[h], "dow=", dow[h], "sin=", round(sin[h], 3), "cos=", round(cos[h], 3))
```

which removes the collision:

```
2011-01-01 00:00:00 dow= 5 sin= -0.975 cos= -0.223
2011-01-01 23:00:00 dow= 5 sin= -0.975 cos= -0.223
2011-01-02 00:00:00 dow= 6 sin= -0.782 cos= 0.623
2011-01-02 23:00:00 dow= 6 sin= -0.782 cos= 0.623
2011-01-03 00:00:00 dow= 0 sin= 0.0 cos= 1.0
```


## Environment

- `tabicl` version: 2.1.1 (`tabicl[forecast]`)
- Installed via PyPI
- Python 3.12
- `gluonts` (installed as a dependency of `tabicl[forecast]`)

If you want to, I can propose a fix and create a pull request.

title: Clarification on feature grouping training when final feature counts differ after delete_unique_features
body:
Hi, thank you again for open-sourcing TabICLv2 and the PR #111 graph_scm prior.

I am trying to reproduce a smaller-scale TabICLv2 classification pretraining run using PR #111, with the v2 feature grouping path enabled (`col_feature_group=same`).

While wiring the training loop, I noticed a potential ambiguity around variable final feature counts (`d`) after prior generation.

From the current code:

- `ColEmbedding.forward` asserts that `d is None` when feature grouping is enabled:
  `assert d is None, "d is not supported when feature grouping is enabled."`
- the trainer aligns each micro-batch by truncating `micro_X` to `micro_d.max()`, then calls:
  `self.model(micro_X, y_train, micro_d)`
- `TabICL._train_forward` only sets `d=None` when all `d` values are identical and equal to the current feature dimension `H`.

I initially thought setting `batch_size_per_gp` / `batch_size_per_subgp` equal to the per-rank micro-batch size would solve this, since the prior samples one shared `num_features` per subgroup. However, `delete_unique_features` removes constant features independently per generated dataset and updates the final `d`.

In a small prior-only diagnostic with the Stage-1-like setting:

- global batch size: 66
- simulated world size: 6
- per-rank batch / micro-batch size: 11
- `batch_size_per_gp=11`
- `batch_size_per_subgp=11`
- `col_feature_group=same`
- `graph_scm` prior with filtering enabled

I found that even though the sampled `num_features` is shared within the micro-batch, the final `d` after `delete_unique_features` often differs across datasets.

For example:

```text
[55, 44, 55, 55, 55, 53, 55, 55, 55, 53, 53]
[49, 47, 50, 50, 50, 49, 50, 50, 50, 50, 50]
[38, 45, 32, 50, 50, 34, 47, 50, 36, 50, 50]
```

In my small diagnostic:

- with `min_features=5,max_features=100`, 46/50 micro-batches had mixed final `d`;
- with fixed `min_features=max_features=50`, 49/50 micro-batches still had mixed final `d`.

So I wanted to ask:

1. In the paper-aligned TabICLv2 pretraining recipe with feature grouping enabled, how do you handle this final `d` mismatch after `delete_unique_features`?
2. Is the intended solution to use `micro_batch_size=1` / per-dataset forward with gradient accumulation?
3. Or do you bucket/regroup generated datasets by final `d` before the model forward?

This matters because the public PR111 trainer seems to work only when each feature-grouping forward receives `d=None`, but the current prior can produce mixed final `d` within a micro-batch even when sampled `num_features` is shared.

Thank you!

title: Add predict_logits to TabICLClassifier
body:
Thank you very much for our great work! Really appreciating it! 
I was looking for an option to output logits or log odds with the TabICLClassifier. Similar to decision_function in logistic regression in scikit learn. This is important since explaining the feature contributions in TabICLClassifiers with shap/shapiq in logits isolates true feature interactions driven by the model's logic. 
In contrariety, probability output (predict_proba) introduces mathematical interaction artifacts by the probability boundary. E.g. if two features push a prediction toward 100%, their combined probability cannot exceed 1.0. shap/shapiq will interpret this mathematical capping as a negative interaction between the features, even if the model treats them as completely independent internally.
Hence, I propose to implement a TabICLClassifier.predict_logits(X) similar to scikit learn or TabPFN. Thank you in advance!

title: sklearn `check_is_fitted` gives wrong result for unfitted TabICL estimator after it is unpickled
body:
in `__setstate__` [here](https://github.com/soda-inria/tabicl/blob/86b12f989fb6a1bab2b09e4a867a37a91366ae2d/src/tabicl/_sklearn/base.py#L302) , the `device_` and `model_` are always created, even if the original serialized model was not fitted and did not have those attributes

```
>>> from tabicl import TabICLClassifier
>>> import pickle

>>> c = TabICLClassifier(device="cpu", random_state=42) # has no device_
>>> pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(c)).device_ # or equivalently copy.deepcopy(c).device_
device(type='cpu')
```

because the estimator does not define `__sklearn_is_fitted__`, this can fool scikit-learn's `check_is_fitted` into thinking the deserialized model is fitted even though it is not.

It might be advisable to inspect some other attribute or a flag inserted in the state and only set the device_ and checkpoint if they existed before serialization. alternatively `__sklearn_is_fitted__` could be defined and check a fitted attribute that is known to be reliable

title: Fix: allow NaN input in preprocessing pipeline
body:
## Summary

`TabICLClassifier.fit()` raises `ValueError: Input X contains NaN` despite the README documenting mean imputation for missing numerical values.

The `PreprocessingPipeline` correctly includes a `SimpleImputer` for numeric columns (line 118 of `preprocessing.py`), but `validate_data()` calls throughout the preprocessing chain reject NaN **before** the imputer has a chance to run.

## Reproduction

```python
import numpy as np
from tabicl import TabICLClassifier

X = np.array([[1.0, 2.0], [4.0, np.nan], [7.0, 8.0]], dtype=np.float32)
y = np.array(["a", "b", "a"])

clf = TabICLClassifier(device="cpu", n_estimators=1)
clf.fit(X, y)  # ValueError: Input X contains NaN.
```

## Root cause

`validate_data()` in `sklearn_utils.py` is called by `EnsembleGenerator`, `UniqueFeatureFilter`, `OutlierRemover`, `CustomStandardScaler`, and `PreprocessingPipeline` — all **before** the `SimpleImputer` in the `ColumnTransformer` runs. sklearn's `check_array` rejects NaN by default.

## Fix

One-line change: set `force_all_finite="allow-nan"` as the default in `validate_data()`. This is safe because the `SimpleImputer` handles NaN downstream, and the remaining preprocessors (`OutlierRemover`, `CustomStandardScaler`) already use `np.nanmean`/`np.nanstd`.

Note: `force_all_finite` was renamed to `ensure_all_finite` in sklearn 1.6. Since tabicl supports `scikit-learn>=1.3.0`, this PR uses the older name for backwards compatibility.

## Testing

Verified locally with tabicl 2.0.3 + scikit-learn 1.6.1:
- NaN input: fit/predict works correctly after fix
- Clean input: no change in behavior

title: Proposal: post-hoc centering of SHAP
body:
Dear TabICL maintainers,

I was reading the [SHAP Tutorial](https://tabicl.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/interpretability.html) and noticed a potential issue with the current SHAP implementation regarding the baseline bias.
I'd like to propose a lightweight, post-hoc correction to improve the readability of the feature attributions without adding inference overhead.

Currently, the baseline $\phi_0$ appears to be based on the prediction for an "all-NaN" input, i.e., $f(\text{all NaN})$. If this value deviates significantly from the true expected prediction over the dataset ($E[f(X)]$), this discrepancy gets absorbed into the individual SHAP values $\phi_i$.

As a result, the SHAP values for certain features become systematically biased (e.g., unidirectionally pushing predictions up or down regardless of the actual feature value). This can distort the interpretation, especially the SHAP importance measure.

I propose applying a post-hoc centering to the already computed SHAP values. We can simply center the SHAP values and shift the base value accordingly:
1. Center the SHAP values for each feature: $$\phi_i^*(x) = \phi_i(x) - E[\phi_i(X)]$$
2. Adjust the base value to absorb the shift: $$\phi_0^* = \phi_0 + \sum_{i=1}^M E[\phi_i(X)]$$

This can be easily implemented by adding three lines in the definition of `get_shap_values()`
```{Python}
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", message=".*does not have valid feature names.*")
        sv = explainer(X_np)
    # proposed addition --------
    average_shap = sv.values.mean(axis=0)
    sv.values -= average_shap
    sv.base_values += average_shap.sum(axis=0)
    # --------
    if attribute_names is not None and hasattr(sv, "feature_names"):
```

FYI: [kaggle notebook for comparison](https://www.kaggle.com/code/negoto/iml-xai-with-tabicl)

However, if this baseline behavior is an intentional design choice that reflects the specific nature of TabICL's predictions, please feel free to disregard this suggestion. I just wanted to share this insight in case it helps improve the interpretability of the model.

It would be highly appreciated if you could let me know what you think!
